body:
The block that fills the 68 `__meta_rds_cluster_*` labels sat inside the loop over the instances of the cluster, so a cluster with 16 instances built it 16 times from the same `types.DBCluster`. It is now built once into `commonLabels`
and copied into each target, the way `addCacheClusterTargets` already does for ElastiCache nodes.

The last instance of a cluster takes ownership of `commonLabels` instead of copying them, which keeps a single-instance cluster at its previous cost.

Labels are unchanged.

Most of the diff in `rds.go` is the re-indent of the 212 moved lines and `labels` becoming `commonLabels`; `git diff -w` shows what actually changed.

## Benchmarks

`go test ./discovery/aws/ -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkRDSRefresh -benchmem -count=6`, against a fixture populated the way the RDS API populates a provisioned Aurora PostgreSQL cluster.

```
                                    │     before      │                after                │
                                    │     sec/op      │    sec/op     vs base               │
RDSRefresh/1Cluster/1Instance-12        9.003µ ± 3%     8.821µ ± 53%        ~ (p=0.065 n=6)
RDSRefresh/1Cluster/16Instances-12      88.74µ ± 2%     68.66µ ±  6%  -22.63% (p=0.002 n=6)
RDSRefresh/20Clusters/4Instances-12     310.6µ ± 2%     276.1µ ±  3%  -11.11% (p=0.002 n=6)
geomean                                 62.84µ          55.09µ        -12.33%

                                    │      B/op       │                B/op                 │
RDSRefresh/1Cluster/1Instance-12       16.00Ki ± 0%    16.03Ki ± 0%         ~ (p=0.102 n=6)
RDSRefresh/1Cluster/16Instances-12     200.4Ki ± 0%    165.2Ki ± 0%  -17.57% (p=0.002 n=6)
RDSRefresh/20Clusters/4Instances-12   1137.1Ki ± 0%    994.8Ki ± 0%  -12.51% (p=0.002 n=6)
geomean                                153.9Ki         138.1Ki       -10.28%

                                    │    allocs/op    │              allocs/op              │
RDSRefresh/1Cluster/1Instance-12         62.00 ± 0%      62.00 ± 0%        ~ (p=1.000 n=6)
RDSRefresh/1Cluster/16Instances-12       656.0 ± 0%      341.0 ± 0%  -48.02% (p=0.002 n=6)
RDSRefresh/20Clusters/4Instances-12     3.398k ± 0%     2.137k ± 0%  -37.11% (p=0.002 n=6)
geomean                                  517.0           356.2       -31.11%
```

No case regresses. A single-instance cluster is unchanged, which is what the ownership handover above is for: without it the extra map cost that case +9% `sec/op` and +13% `B/op`.

## Tests

`TestRDSDiscoveryRefresh` reimplemented target construction instead of calling `refresh`, so it asserted its own copy of the label logic. The copy had already drifted: it built `__address__` from the instance endpoint port, while `refresh` builds it from the configured `port`. It now calls `refresh` and compares complete label sets, so it fails when a label is added, dropped or changed.

```release-notes
[PERF] AWS SD: Build RDS cluster labels once per cluster instead of once per instance.
```
title: discovery/aws: build RDS cluster labels once per cluster
